result.title: Wavenumber-Aware Deep Learning for Robust Analysis of Raman Spectra
result.comment: 29 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables; Supplementary Information (15 pages) included
result.summary: Machine-learning models for spectroscopy usually treat a spectrum as a fixed-grid intensity vector, leaving the physical coordinate implicit in the array index. Such models are tied to a single sampling grid, spectral range and resolution, which limits their use when measurement conditions change. Here we represent each spectral point as a pair of intensity and wavenumber and compute Transformer positional encodings from the wavenumber itself. On Raman spectra of three bacterial species and their synthetic mixtures, this representation remained robust to noise, sparser sampling and partial spectral coverage across convolutional, residual and Transformer networks. In controlled comparisons, wavenumber-based encoding outperformed index-based and learned encodings under partial observation and retained its performance on sampling grids never seen during training, where index-based encoding degraded. These findings were reproduced on a public 30-isolate bacterial benchmark. Explicit physical coordinates offer a simple route to robust spectral analysis under variable measurement conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 该文将光谱每个点表示为「强度—波数」对，并把波数本身作为 Transformer 位置编码的输入，在细菌拉曼光谱及公开基准上验证其在噪声、稀疏采样和部分谱覆盖下比索引编码更稳健。
AI.relevance_reason: 把位置编码由数组索引改为物理坐标、从而在未见采样网格上保持性能的思路，可能为 LVR 中位置编码、长度泛化以及 latent 相似度里位置/深度因素的解耦提供可借鉴的问题表述。
